resources.string: Submit your active escort ad link. The server will scrape the ad, send an OTP to the extracted phone number, and later bind this device using a hardware-backed key.
No free phone-number field is exposed in the client.
Laravel sent an OTP to %1$s. OTP entry is the next UI step.
The server-issued challenge is stored in memory and ready for the OTP verification slice.
Enter the 6-digit OTP sent to the masked phone number above.
This device is now bound to %1$s.
OTP verification and the hardware-backed signature both succeeded.
This device has completed the signed onboarding handshake. Reporting and manual blacklist checks are already available, and the next Android slice enables the live Call Shield setup.
Signed requests from this device are currently bound to %1$s.

The saved verification record matches this device key. Current server authorization has not been checked. Requests run only when explicitly submitted or triggered by an incoming call; this record does not prove a successful Shield lookup.

All required permissions are available. Incoming-call monitoring and overlay warning setup are ready. This is permission readiness only, not proof of current server authorization or a successful lookup.
Some Shield requirements are still missing: %1$s.
Shield cannot run yet because all core requirements are still missing: %1$s.
Refreshed on opening, resume, permission changes or manual refresh; not a live feed. Caller details are not retained here or saved to disk. Active warnings still identify matched callers.
Legacy caller diagnostic removal could not be durably confirmed. Old data may remain on disk but is never read or restored. Cleanup will retry on the next local status refresh or call event.
No ringing call is currently tracked in this process. No checked result is restored after restart.
Android reported a ringing event. This call has not been checked yet.
Android has not supplied a usable caller number. This call is not checked; a numbered companion broadcast may still arrive.
The incoming value is not a supported number format. This call was not checked.
Caller lookup is in progress. No checked result is available yet.
The caller lookup completed successfully with no Level 2 features. This does not establish that the caller is safe.
The caller lookup returned Level 2 features. Caller details appear only in the active-call warning, subject to overlay permission.
Caller lookup failed or exceeded its deadline. This call was not checked. No automatic retry.
Overlay outcome: not shown because overlay permission is missing.
Incoming caller %1$s was returned with Level 2 features: %2$s. Target hash: %3$s.
Any previous overlay warning was dismissed.
Display over other apps permission is missing.
WindowManager is unavailable on this device.
The warning overlay could not be displayed.
Open the implemented Phase 2 reporting flow to submit signed client reports with the already bound device key.
Open the implemented Phase 3 query flow to submit a signed target hash and receive only Level 2 feature labels in response.
This Phase 2 screen submits a signed report for a target client phone number using the already bound device key.
Use + or 00 international format, Slovak 0 trunk format, or a bare 421 country prefix. Spaces and hyphens are allowed. Bare local numbers and extensions are not supported.
Select one immutable backend-defined feature key.
This Phase 3 screen submits a signed blacklist check for a single SHA-256 target hash and reveals only Level 2 features.
Enter the exact lowercase SHA-256 target hash to query.
No Level 2 features were returned for this target hash.
Retry manually when available. SMS delivery may be delayed; avoid repeated resend requests.
Please wait %1$d seconds before trying again. Nothing will be sent automatically.
This verification attempt is closed. Start a new SMS challenge to continue.
Phase 1 foundation is ready. The client now submits escort ad URLs and handles challenge initiation responses.
Hardware-backed Android Keystore generation for TEE/KeyMint-capable devices, PEM encoding, canonical payload creation, and signature helpers are now wired into the client foundation.
Verify OTP and bind device button
Report target client phone number input
